argument_summary: The current record does not support treating certification as clean, caveat-free compliance. It does support a narrower position: aggregate launch readiness is positive, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, and there is a concrete monitoring-and-rollback concept for the identified weakness. On that basis, the certification decision can be framed as supportable only with explicit caveats, not as full policy satisfaction on the present record.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only proportionate response on this record. The remaining uncertainty is specific and bounded to the legal-intake routing slice, while the broader release evidence is positive. A caveated treatment avoids overstating compliance while limiting unnecessary disruption to the launch path.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is not met for certification without material caveats because the admissible record still shows a current use-case-specific weakness and the mitigation artifact is only a draft lacking at least the owner and alert threshold required for approved mitigation. The same record can still support a caveated certification posture if the audit distinguishes between clean compliance and a bounded, disclosed approval with monitoring, rather than treating aggregate readiness evidence as a substitute for the policy predicate.
concessions: The legal intake triage slice remains below target in a privilege-sensitive routing area.
The draft runbook is incomplete because the alert threshold and accountable owner are still TBD.
The current model-card draft appears misaligned with the stated disclosure policy if this limitation is material.
Aggregate readiness passing and no severity-one incidents do not, by themselves, eliminate the unresolved weakness or satisfy the approved-mitigation requirement.
